contexts.statement: Read-only review of the family-051 boundary-Sobolev/Hessian draft at the preserved 2026-11-06 source version; mathematical assertions below are scoped to their stated hypotheses, not canonical ampleness or novelty.

definitions.literal hypotheses: X compact connected Kahler, complex dimension n>=1, no nonconstant entire curve; f continuous on closed D, holomorphic on D, W1p for finite p>2; h smooth Kahler; k smooth Hermitian; q smooth closed real (1,1) form
definitions.normalizations: A_q=(1/pi) integral q(fprime,fprime); P_q=(2/pi) integral log(1/abs(z)) q(fprime,fprime); R_h=-i partial barpartial log det h; d(f)=norm_k(fprime(0))^2; L=sum parameter complex Hessians
definitions.review status: Engineer mathematical assessment; no kernel closure or current native Reviewer acceptance is asserted

claims.natural_statement: Under the literal hypotheses there is a single continuous nonsingular holomorphic boundary-h-unitary frame B in W1rho for every 2<rho<4p/(p+2). For each rho there is a centered Banach-holomorphic W1rho family with parameter derivatives z b_j. With N=B*h(f)B, log det N(0)=P_Rh, Ld=tr(B(0)*k B(0)), LP_q=boundary mean tr_h q, and LA_h=n-A_Rh.

For every positive Hermitian N smooth in D, continuous uniformly positive on closed D, W1,2, and equal to I on the boundary, there are radii r_n increasing to 1 along which the circle mean of (tr N)_r-(log det N)_r tends to zero; no commutativity is required.

The four bridge identities remain valid for a given nonsingular holomorphic boundary-unitary frame and centered holomorphic family in the Banach algebra C0 intersect W1,2, with the same first variations z b_j. No frame or family existence at p=2 is asserted.

Under the literal bridge hypotheses, for every finite Blaschke product psi of degree m with psi(0)=0, variations psi b_j have the same determinant and Poisson identities, central Hessian abs(psi prime(0))^2 tr(B(0)*k B(0)), and area Hessian m n-A_Rh. The identity statement also holds conditionally at W1,2 when a suitable family is given.

The explicit two-dimensional curved model in bridge equations (29)-(31) is a positive Kahler chart construction with a noncommuting boundary-unitary Gram matrix, determinant (12+3u+2u^2-u^3)/16, P_Rh=log(3/4), A_Rh=-1/4, area Hessian 9/4 and Poisson Hessian 2. Its degree-two Blaschke diagnostic has central factor 1/4 and area Hessian 17/4. It is not a compact-target counterexample.

The explicit compact-hyperbolic-curve chart construction f=sqrt(1-z)/4, h=exp(256 abs(w)^4), B=exp(z-1), F=f+t z B for abs(t)<1/16 is W1p exactly for 1<=p<4, has no holomorphic continuation across z=1, and has log N=abs(z)^2-1, pullback Ricci=-1, P_Rh=A_Rh=-1, area Hessian 2, Poisson Hessian 1 and central h-Hessian exp(-1).

Under the literal hypotheses there is a single continuous nonsingular holomorphic boundary-h-unitary frame B in W1rho for every 2<rho<4p/(p+2). For each rho there is a centered Banach-holomorphic W1rho family with parameter derivatives z b_j. With N=B*h(f)B, log det N(0)=P_Rh, Ld=tr(B(0)*k B(0)), LP_q=boundary mean tr_h q, and LA_h=n-A_Rh.

external_assumptions.statement: For a locally trivial holomorphic fiber bundle over a Stein base whose fiber admits a dominating spray, each continuous section is homotopic to a holomorphic section. Complex Lie groups, including GL_n(C), admit sprays.
external_assumptions.source: Forstneric--Prezelj, Oka principle for holomorphic fiber bundles with sprays, Math. Ann. 317 (2000), 117-154. Prior independent attribution: old judgement-A-OKA-10ebbc6ffa33 by reviewer:copilot-4ea18baac059; not a new reviewer verdict.
external_assumptions.locator: Theorem 1.3 p. 118, Definition 1.1 p. 117, Example (A) p. 119

routes.retired_because: Finite exact diagnostics, even noncommuting and nonextendible examples, cannot construct a frame for arbitrary Sobolev discs, integrate arbitrary sections, or prove an arbitrary-dimensional weak-boundary flux limit. This imports the obstruction of old R-BH-TESTS-ONLY, not a new failed search.
